彩.meaning: A cat with long <part>whiskers</part> rolls the <part>dice</part> to pick a paint pot, one for red and six for gold, dips her whiskers in and flicks them across the white hallway. By lunch the walls are a rainbow, and the landlord is furious about her <kanji>coloring</kanji>.
彩.on: She rinses her whiskers in a jug of <sound>ci</sound>der before the next roll.
彩.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' squeaks a <sound>ro</sound>dent as she paints its tail to match a <sound>do</sound>lphin poster.

屈.meaning: At the castle <part>exit</part>, the guard's <part>flag</part> is too tall for the low door, so every morning it jams and the whole parade backs up. At last the flagpole gives in and folds itself in half to squeeze through. Even wood knows when to <kanji>yield</kanji>.
屈.on: A <sound>coo</sound>t perches on the folded pole and bows to everyone who passes.
屈.kun: Behind it, a <sound>ca</sound>rp ducks low under the door with a string of <sound>ga</sound>rlic on its head.

炎.meaning: A doctor examines a camper's swollen red ankle. It's so hot that a <part>fire</part> is burning on top of it, and a second fire is perched on top of that. 'Classic,' she says, roasting a marshmallow over it. 'Very bad <kanji>inflammation</kanji>.'
炎.on: The ambulance's <sound>en</sound>gine overheats just driving past.
炎.kun: She cooks a <sound>ho</sound>tdog on the flames too, wailing '<sound>No</sound>, <sound>oh</sound> no!' as it chars.

幅.meaning: A greedy bear spots a <part>cookie jar</part> through the kitchen door, but he's too fat to fit. He holds a <part>towel</part> across the doorway to measure it, then across himself, and sighs. The problem is clearly his own <kanji>width</kanji>.
幅.on: So he fishes the jar out through the window with a long <sound>hook</sound>.
幅.kun: He eats the cookies outside his <sound>hu</sound>t, next to the <sound>ba</sound>rbecue, where there are no doors at all.

卒.meaning: After <part>ten</part> long years at clown school, the <part>twins</part> toss their caps in the air, but someone has glued both caps to one saucepan <part>lid</part>, so it clangs back down on both heads at once. Everyone cheers anyway. They <kanji>graduate</kanji>.
卒.on: They collapse on a <sound>so</sound>fa and sneeze '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' from all the confetti.
卒.kun: '<sound>So</sound>!' snaps the head clown, cutting the speech dead and shooing them off the stage.

宣.meaning: A chef climbs onto the <part>roof</part> of his diner, holds the world's tallest <part>burger</part> over his head and bellows to the whole street: 'Free fries for anyone who can finish it!' Pigeons gather. He loves to <kanji>proclaim</kanji> things from up there.
宣.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try across the road salutes and asks for extra pickles.
宣.kun: '<sound>No</sound>!' shouts a <sound>ta</sound>co seller below, banging a <sound>mu</sound>g on his cart.

繰.meaning: Kids in a <part>treehouse</part> lower a basket on a long <part>thread</part> to the snack shop below, then turn a creaky crank to haul it back up: biscuits, comics, a grumpy cat. Round and round goes the handle. Their whole day is spent <kanji>winding</kanji>.
繰.on: One basket comes back with nothing but a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p from their mum.
繰.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo nests on the crank and pops out every time it turns.
